loom: Loom — vendor-neutral agent memory plane on ClickHouse.

positional arguments: {code,decisions,export-okf,import-okf,okf-lint,up,down,ch-setup,participant,deployment,settings,secrets,signing-key,provider-lock,export-analytics,reembed,reextract,deploy-delta,entity-export,audit-namespace,mentor,serve,migrate,reconcile-status,period-digest,demote-activity-narration,recalibrate,import-clickgap,import-recall,import-brain,claim-release,mint-token,revoke-token,sso,bot,doctor,report,drops,namespaces-gc,erasure-re-verify,tracker-probe,tracker-contract-check,tracker-dupcheck-fit,tracker-embed-reset,namespaces-adopt,sensitivity-sweep,integrity-repair,rechunk,export-actions,lexical-stats-rebuild,version,install,demo,init,ingest-transcript,memory-search,set-host,login,logout,whoami,call,token} code Code intelligence plane operations. decisions Decision records mined from documents. export-okf Render a namespace as an OKF v0.2 bundle (Markdown + frontmatter) — the git-reviewable projection of Loom memory. import-okf Write the concepts of an OKF v0.2 bundle into a namespace via memory.set. okf-lint Lint an OKF bundle directory offline — the compile gate a mirror repository's CI runs. Exit 2 critical, 1 warnings, 0 clean. up Boot the local stack (Loom + ClickHouse) and print how to connect: creates .env and the ClickHouse config from their templates, runs docker compose up --build, waits for /v1/health, then prints the dashboard URL and the first memory.set (curl + Python SDK) and `claude mcp add` snippets — minting a writer token first when auth is on. Re-run any time. down Stop the local stack while preserving data; --delete-data performs a confirmed reset. ch-setup Prepare a self-managed ClickHouse or a ClickHouse Cloud service for Loom: create the loom database and the read-only reader user, or print the SQL for an admin. participant The Loom processes a provider change waits for. deployment The configuration every replica checks itself against. settings Every setting's value in force, and overrides of the live ones. secrets Credentials and signing keys stored sealed in ClickHouse. signing-key The token signing keys beside LOOM_JWT_SECRET, kept in ClickHouse. provider-lock The provider configuration lock. export-analytics Write one UTC day of usage and a namespace snapshot to S3 as Parquet, names hashed under LOOM_ANALYTICS_EXPORT_NAME_KEY. Never replaces an object, so a repeated run is safe. reembed Re-embed vectors whose embedding_model != the configured embedder (run after changing LOOM_EMBEDDING_MODEL — Loom does not auto-re-embed). Covers memory, entity, and conversation vectors. Coded vector tables keep their width: change a model of another width in Settings → Models & keys, which rebuilds them. reextract Replay a namespace's raw evidence (memory.set_from_messages turns) through a running server's write path into ANOTHER namespace — the current extractor over the stored transcripts; the source is never written. deploy-delta What a colour swap changed: the deployment's ledger rows (volume, errors, p50/p95, upstream spend per operation) and its ClickHouse statement shapes (runs, bytes, seconds) for a window on each side of the swap, with flags for what moved past a coarse threshold. entity-export Export a namespace's entity graph (co-occurrence edges + triples) to GraphML or JSON-LD for an external graph or RDF tool. Read-only; every edge carries its provenance and a note that a path is declared, not proven. audit-namespace How a namespace is being used (namespace.audit): exact-key reads vs searches, hash keys, double-encoded and oversized values, hand-rolled index rows, leases stored as memories, version churn. Read-only; prints a table (code, severity, kind, count, share, first sample) or --json. Exit 1 on a critical finding. mentor The store's advice to one agent (mentor.brief): what it called, the planes its namespace offers, the hints with their evidence, and how often past hints were followed. Read-only; prints a table or --json. Exit 1 when a warning-level hint fires. serve Boot the control plane (uvicorn). migrate Apply schema migrations against the configured CH. reconcile-status Re-emit memory_embeddings rows whose status diverged from loom.memory (superseded / conflicted / duplicate marks the pool never saw), compared and re-emitted per identity row (org, namespace, agent, user_id, session_id, key). Dry run by default (counts by status, the rows it would write); --apply writes. period-digest Write period digests — one derived episodic memory over K consecutive session digests of each identity in one namespace. Additive and idempotent. Dry run by default (plans only); --apply writes. demote-activity-narration Find a namespace's extracted facts that narrate tool activity ('User read lines 1-1000 of X', 'Claude ran a command on …') with no durable outcome and demote (confidence x0.25) or label them through memory.apply. Dry run by default; keys an agent read by name in the last --days are left alone. Never deletes. recalibrate Re-probe the embedder + run per-NS calibration immediately (otherwise this runs weekly via the recalibration worker). import-clickgap Import a ClickGap (Detector→Validator→Reviewer) SQLite export into Loom (lessons + typed entities + categories). Reembed-only; preserves kind→memory_type, per-row TTL, recall_count (→ ranking via reinforcement_count), suppression polarity, and provenance. Idempotent via deterministic keys + per-run version. import-recall Import an external vector-recall agent-memory SQLite export into Loom. Introspects the DB at runtime (schema not assumed): tables are classified by column heuristics into memories (→ memory.set) or conversation transcripts (→ conversation.append, grouped by conversation id); unmatched tables/rows are skipped, never crash. Idempotent via deterministic keys. import-brain Import a markdown agent 'brain' directory into Loom: MEMORY.md (always- injected HOT layer) → profile.set sections; memory/contexts/*.md (read-on- demand WARM layer) → knowledge.add docs. Completes the migration alongside import-recall (the deep vector layer). Missing files are skipped, never crash. claim-release Release a self-signup claim: revoke its grants, clear the owner, deactivate it. The name stays reserved. mint-token Mint a JWT locally (requires LOOM_JWT_SECRET). revoke-token Revoke one token by jti or subject (writes loom.revoked_tokens through the revocation module; needs the configured ClickHouse). sso Carry password accounts over to single sign-on. bot Bots and CI jobs that sign in with a key or their CI's identity. doctor Diagnose pre-boot misconfig (Python version, settings, JWT, CH reachability) and print the problem list /v1/health carries, each with its fix. With --client, also examine this machine as a coding-agent client. report Print the bug form's Environment field: versions and the `loom doctor` checks. drops Print the memory ingest drop ledger (loom.memory_drops) for a namespace, by stage/reason — what the pipeline discarded, truncated or gave up on. namespaces-gc List (default) or erase throwaway namespaces — finished bench runs under the bench prefixes that nobody registered and nobody has written to for --idle-hours — in one list-scoped erasure saga per batch. erasure-re-verify Re-verify failed erasure sagas: print each one's last step-named reason and a fresh residue census (default, read-only); --resume re-runs them from their checkpoint past the recovery worker's attempts budget; --orphan-graph lists namespaces whose entity graph outlived their memories and, with --erase, purges them. tracker-probe Read-only first contact with the tracker source: counts and newest timestamps per upstream table per credential, breaker states, the configured tracker namespaces. tracker-contract-check Read-only: does each tracker source's schema meet the record contract (docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md)? Names missing tables / columns, optional tables present, feature columns. Exit 0 when every checked source meets it. tracker-dupcheck-fit Refit tracker.duplicate_check's calibrated confidence for one tracker namespace now: replays the duplicate gold at filing time, fits, stores the fit. tracker-embed-reset Clear the tracker_embed pass cursors of one tracker namespace so the next pass re-walks the window and re-embeds every item whose text recipe changed. Dry run by default (prints the cursors); --apply clears them. namespaces-adopt Give namespaces that hold live memory and no registry row an owner row: kind=bench under the bench prefixes, else memory; retention_days 0, no TTL. Dry run unless --apply. sensitivity-sweep Label live rows the sensitivity detector would have labelled on write but a path skipped. Dry run by default: counts by level, probe shape and namespace. --apply writes one new version per row, tombstones a high row's embedding rows and tags a medium row's. The closing line is the high- sensitivity invariant (high rows with a live embedding). integrity-repair Read the row-level integrity gauges (dim-0 rows holding a vector, tombstoned_at/status drift, active rows past valid_to) and, with --apply, re-emit the dim-0 rows with their true dimension so search can return them again. Drift and valid_to are listed, not repaired. rechunk Re-chunk and re-embed a namespace's knowledge documents from stored content through the current chunker, so every document carries section metadata and document frequency. Idempotent; one embedding per new chunk. Dry run by default (counts the documents and chunks); --apply re-chunks. export-actions Export the action schema derived from the operation registry — an MCP tools/list manifest with loom extras (json) or the Cedar schema (cedar) a policy gateway governs the surface with. lexical-stats-rebuild Recompute BM25 document frequency for a namespace from its live rows (the term-frequency views only see inserts; supersession and tombstones leave stale vocabulary behind). version Print installed Loom version. install Wire Loom into a local AI client's config. Writes the MCP server block into Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code's config file, atomically, merging with anything already there; for Claude Code it runs (or prints) `claude mcp add` and for Codex `codex mcp add`. Restart the client afterwards. demo The first five minutes: ingest this repo's AGENTS.md (or --file) into the knowledge plane the way `make ingest` does, ask it a question, and print the answer with its evidence rows. On the stock fake-LLM stack it prints the top knowledge.search hits and says what a real answer needs. init Create an identity on a Loom server. `--agent NAME` signs an agent up by itself (server needs LOOM_SELF_SIGNUP=open): mints a writer token on a fresh agent-<slug> namespace, saves it to ~/.loom/token, and prints the one-time code a person uses in the dashboard to claim the namespace. ingest-transcript Pipe a chat-history file (markdown / JSON) into Loom's conversation table as one thread. Generic ingest for tools without an MCP integration (Aider, Continue.dev, JetBrains AI, anything else): export the chat → run this command → the thread shows in the dashboard's Conversations. memory-search Run a memory.search from the shell. Default human output; --json-agent emits a structured envelope agents can pipe through (a `{command, results}` JSON shape). set-host Designate the Loom host(s) for this deployment. Writes the given login handle(s) or email(s) to LOOM_PLATFORM_ADMINS in the .env (--env-file, default ./.env): a handle promotes that password account to platform_admin, an email promotes an SSO sign-in with that verified email. Multiple OK (on-call rotation, co-operators, etc.). Re-login required after to pick up the role. login Sign in to a Loom server on any browser with a one-time code. logout End the stored session on the server and forget it here. whoami Show who the stored session signs you in as. call Call any operation or API route with the stored session (`loom call --help`). token Make, list and revoke your own tokens for CI and agents (`loom token --help`).

loom code: positional arguments: {init,backfill,reconcile,compact,reembed,vector-twin,crossref,coverage-import,export-pairs,backfill-prs,repack,describe,answers-purge,scip-full,scip-lock-path,entry-lock,scip-delta,entries,warm,scip-retry,backfill-reviews,backfill-assignees,backfill-items,stats,export-matrix,lint-instructions} init Create the bare clone + seed state. backfill Full-tree indexing (resumable). reconcile Content-based staleness check: paths whose chunks predate their last change at the branch head; --heal re-ingests them (watermark untouched). compact OPTIMIZE ... FINAL a code vector table when its physical copies per key reach --min-ratio, and wait for the merge. Dry run by default (measures the ratio); --apply optimizes. reembed Write the namespace's live chunks under a second embedding model's label: in-database, resumable, no checkout. vector-twin Fill a namespace's Matryoshka-prefix twin of the chunk vectors inside ClickHouse: no re-embed, resumable. crossref SQL/shell test -> implementing C++ reference pass (writes code_test_map method=content_reference; idempotent). coverage-import Import the newest per-test line coverage run of the configured source (writes code_test_map method=coverage and code_coverage_files). export-pairs Export (query -> acted-on unit, hard negatives) retrieval pairs from real traffic (trace x outcome join) for embedder/reranker fine-tuning. backfill-prs Merged-PR history from GitHub. repack Regenerate context packs for recently merged PRs in the current pack shape. describe LLM contextual one-liners for top-PageRank chunks. answers-purge Tombstone cached code.ask answers (after a synthesis-model upgrade, stale weaker-model answers would otherwise be served forever — the cache only self-invalidates on cited-file change). Dry run by default (counts and samples the matches); --apply tombstones. scip-full Full compiler-tier re-index by hand (the code_scip_full worker runs it weekly by default: heals the TU-cap degrades of per-merge deltas and any drift). Heavy: ~50 min of scip-clang + apply, on this host rather than in the server. scip-lock-path Print the entry's compiler-tier lock file on this host. A manual harness run goes under `loom code entry-lock`, which takes this file and the deployment lease; scip-full and scip-delta take both themselves. entry-lock Run a command under the entry's compiler-tier lock (this host's file and the deployment's lease): exit 75 when another pass holds it, 3 when the lease is lost mid-run (the command is stopped). scip-delta One compiler-tier delta pass (same code as the code_scip_delta worker), by hand: git_head vs scip_commit per configured repo, scip-clang over the changed TUs, apply. Prints `RESULT: ...`. entries One line per configured repository: org namespace checkout lock-file (the lock path resolved; a manual run takes it through `loom code entry-lock`). warm Pre-seed the code.ask answer cache from a question list (one question per line, or JSONL with a 'question' field). Each miss pays one synthesis; every future asker fleet-wide gets the cached answer. Safe to re-run: hits are free. scip-retry Reset a failed SCIP batch to pending. backfill-reviews Inline review comments for merged PRs already in code_pr_history that have none stored yet (newest first, one GitHub request per PR). backfill-assignees Fill code_pr_history.assignees (who the repo assigned to review) for merged PRs already stored, walking the newest closed PRs 100 per request. backfill-items Fill code_gh_items (issues + PRs, any state) updated since a date, 100 per request, oldest update first; moves gh_items_cursor. stats Watermarks + live row counts. export-matrix Maintenance matrix from merged-PR co-change: 'when this file changes, these usually change too', with evidence, as markdown for an instructions file (AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md). lint-instructions Agent-instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions, .claude/**.md, skills) whose path or symbol references no longer resolve at the clone's head.

loom ch-setup: `loom ch-setup`: prepare a ClickHouse that Loom did not start itself, a self-managed server or a ClickHouse Cloud service, for Loom's first boot. It creates the `loom` database and the read-only reader user (`LOOM_CH_READER_USER`, default `loom_reader`): SELECT on `loom.*` and a settings profile that pins Loom's caller-shaped caps as ceilings, with floors no statement can go under. Run it again at any time: what is in place is left alone, and a reader whose profile or grants differ from that is rebuilt to exactly it, so changes an admin made to the reader do not survive a rerun. A user without the privilege for a step gets the SQL to hand an admin instead, with the password left as a placeholder. The bundled ClickHouse defines the reader in its config, so there it only reports. An existing reader is replaced only when it has the shape ch-setup gives it (a password user on the settings profile of its own name) and logs in with LOOM_CH_PASSWORD; anything else of that name is left alone.

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --subject SUBJECT --org ORG --namespaces NAMESPACES [NAMESPACES ...] Namespace(s) the token covers, space- or comma-separated. Use '*' for wildcard. Mutually exclusive with --namespace-role. --roles {viewer,writer,admin} [{viewer,writer,admin} ...] --platform-admin Mint the platform_admin role, which spans every org, instead of --roles: for a service account (--subject sa:<name>, never an agent's) and with --ttl-days (at most 90); each mint is audited, and the token covers every namespace unless --namespaces names some. --namespace-role NS=ROLE Scoped per-namespace role, repeatable; ARG ORDER = read priority (first = searched first). e.g. --namespace-role priv=admin --namespace-role pub=viewer. Emits an ns_roles claim (a scoped token: restricted to these namespaces, ordered, per-namespace roles). --ttl-days TTL_DAYS Token lifetime in days. Omit for no expiry (the default, kept for dev boxes and `$( )` scripts). Recommended for anything that leaves your machine: --ttl-days 30 and re-mint on a schedule — a token without an exp can only be retired with `loom revoke-token`. --save [PATH] Write the token to PATH (default ~/.loom/token — the file the SDK, `loom import-*`, `loom okf` and the Claude Code hooks read) with mode 0600, creating ~/.loom as 0700, and print the path instead of the token. --read-scope {namespace,own_user,own_session} Widest read this token may make inside its namespaces: namespace (every row, the default), own_user (only rows of the user_id each request names), own_session (only rows of the session_id each request names). Mint own_user for an agent that serves many end users through one token. --read-user-id USER_ID Pin the token to one end user: reads are filtered to this user_id and a request naming another user is refused. --traffic-class {production,interactive,bench} Traffic class every request under this token runs as: its own rate buckets, ClickHouse priority, LLM-tier policy and cost-ledger column. Omit to let the namespace row decide (kind = bench → bench, a registered namespace → production, unknown → interactive). --consumer NAME Bind the consumer tag to this credential: every request under the token is attributed to NAME whatever its body says, and its ledger rows read consumer_source=claimed. Omit to let the request's own `consumer` field (self-reported) or the subject class decide. --service-account Mark token as a service account (default). --user-token Mint as a user token instead of a service account. --json Emit a JSON summary instead of the bare token.
loom revoke-token: usage: loom revoke-token [-h] (--jti JTI | --subject SUBJECT | --list) [--issued-before ISO-8601] [--scim] [--reason REASON] [--expires-at ISO8601] [--json]

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --jti JTI The `jti` claim: retires exactly one token. Every token from `loom mint- token` (printed with --json / --save) and the admin endpoint carries one; a gateway's token may not — use --subject. --subject SUBJECT The `sub` claim: retires EVERY token minted for this principal, in every org (verification checks sub against the revoked set); narrow it with --issued-before. An end user is <org>/user:<id>: their tokens in that org alone. --list Print the unexpired revocations. --issued-before ISO-8601 With --subject: revoke only the tokens issued (`iat`) before this instant, so a token re-minted after a leak keeps working. --scim With --subject and --issued-before: narrow SCIM's revocation of the subject instead of its own, to give back a subject a SCIM deactivation caught that is someone else's. Waits up to 10 s while SCIM is changing the subject. --reason REASON Free text stored on the row (audit trail). --expires-at ISO8601 When the revocation may lapse: no earlier than the last expiry of the tokens it must end (up to a day for a bot allowed one). Omit to keep the row for good (to 2105). --json Machine-readable output.

Its tokens are for sa:<name>; with --agent-claim, each agent the trust's tokens name gets sa:<name>:<agent> and its own namespace <name>-<agent>. list Every bot, active or disabled. disable Refuse its proofs and revoke the tokens it holds.

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --name NAME Its client_id: lower-case letters, digits, '-' --org ORG --namespace-role NS=ROLE viewer|writer|admin on a namespace (repeatable; first = searched first); with --agent-claim, what every agent shares beside its own --generate-key PATH Write a new P-256 private key here (0600) --public-key PATH The bot's own public key, a PEM file (P-256, Ed25519 or RSA) --issuer ISSUER CI trust: the platform's OIDC issuer (https) --audience AUDIENCE CI trust: the audience its token must name --claim NAME=VALUE CI trust: a claim the token must carry; VALUE ending in * matches a prefix (repeatable; at least one, e.g. sub=repo:org/repo:ref:refs/heads/main) --jwks-uri JWKS_URI CI trust: where the issuer publishes its keys (https), when its OIDC discovery is not reachable from Loom --max-token-age SECONDS CI trust: the longest a workload token may live (exp less iat) to be taken --max-access-token-ttl SECONDS The longest token the bot is issued when its request asks (expires_in, 60 to 86400); unasked, a token lives an hour, or this when it is shorter --max-agents MAX_AGENTS With --agent-claim: how many agents the trust may make --agent-claim CLAIM CI trust: the claim naming the agent (e.g. agent_id); each agent gets its own subject and namespace, made on its first sign-in --platform-admin Its tokens carry the platform_admin role, which spans every org; it takes no --namespace-role and no --agent-claim --replace Replace a bot of the same name

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --org ORG Org whose namespaces to scan --prefix PREFIX Namespace prefix (repeatable); default: LOOM_NAMESPACE_BENCH_PREFIXES --namespace NAMESPACE An explicit namespace (repeatable); counted whether its rows are live or tombstoned, so a half-erased namespace can be finished --exclude-prefix EXCLUDE_PREFIX Never touch namespaces under this prefix (repeatable): a reuse set another run reads --idle-hours IDLE_HOURS No write for this long (default 24) --include-registered Also erase namespaces that have a loom.namespaces row --erase Submit the erasure (default: dry run) --no-purge Tombstone instead of deleting the rows (keeps the bytes) --skip-external Loom tables only: skip the external backends (Langfuse traces, ClickStack OTel rows), which erase per namespace and fail closed --batch BATCH Namespaces per saga (default 200) --show SHOW Candidates to print (default 20) --requester REQUESTER --worker-pass Run one pass of the namespace_gc worker instead of the prefix scan: registered kind=bench namespaces with live memory and no write for --idle- hours; --namespace narrows it; dry run unless --erase

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --org ORG Limit to one org (required for --orphan-graph) --id ID Only this erasure id (repeatable) --resume Re-run each failed saga from its steps_completed checkpoint --skip-external With --resume, on namespace_list sagas: loom tables only, skip the external backends whose step kept failing (the ledger's scope object is rewritten) --completed-since ISO_TIMESTAMP Re-verify the completed sagas whose census ran at or after this time, not the failed ones (UTC unless it names an offset): after a rollout, the erasures the previous build ran. Only their orphan row links are counted (entity_triple_rows and entity_edge_rows rows whose memory has no live row and no row written since the census); --resume deletes them --orphan-graph List namespaces holding entity edges with no live memory and no live knowledge chunk --erase With --orphan-graph: purge them in loom-only namespace_list sagas --batch BATCH Namespaces per saga (default 200) --show SHOW Orphan namespaces to print --requester REQUESTER

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --client {claude-desktop,claude-code,codex,cursor,vscode,cline,windsurf,zed} [{claude-desktop,claude-code,codex,cursor,vscode,cline,windsurf,zed} ...] Which client(s) to wire. Omit to auto-detect and wire every supported client found on this machine. --server-url SERVER_URL Loom server URL (default LOOM_BASE_URL, else http://localhost:7777). --token TOKEN JWT to embed in the client config. Defaults to LOOM_API_KEY, then ~/.loom/token. Use `loom mint-token` to generate one. --name NAME Server name: the key under mcpServers (cursor) or servers (vscode), and the name `claude mcp add` / `codex mcp add` registers. --toolset TOOLSET MCP toolset the client lists, as `?toolset=` on the URL: `coding` for a coding agent, empty for the server default (core; claude-code and codex default to `coding`). --dry-run Print what would be written without touching the file. --force claude-code: add the user-scope MCP entry even when the loom plugin is installed (it mounts the server itself; both = every tool listed twice).

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --server-url SERVER_URL Loom server URL (default LOOM_BASE_URL, else http://localhost:7777). --token TOKEN JWT to authenticate with. Defaults to LOOM_API_KEY, then ~/.loom/token. --org ORG default: the token's org, else dev --namespace NAMESPACE Namespace to ingest the thread into. --agent AGENT Agent identifier on the conversation rows (default ingest-cli). --thread-id THREAD_ID Thread to append to (default: a hash of the file's resolved path, so re- ingesting an edited file adds only its new turns). --file FILE Path to the transcript file. Format: markdown with alternating `# user` / `# assistant` H1 sections, OR JSON array of {role, content} objects. --dry-run Parse and print the turn count and each turn's size in bytes (never its text) without writing anything.
